blocks.title: Typography Scales & Inline Rich-Text Palette

paragraphs.text: This opening paragraph uses Level 1 (Hero Lead Scale). Along the Bharathapuzha river corridor, field researchers work with journey-deep, intention-blue, action-blue, dark-gold, and intention-gold spans—connecting readers to curated regional itineraries or jumping smoothly via zero-hash triggers to all six dark interlink banners.

This second paragraph uses Level 2 (Standard Editorial Body Scale), demonstrating earthen accents including terracotta, deep-forest, spiced-copper, dark-peach, and muted archival annotations alongside 14th-century inscriptions and bell-metal alloys (Cu78Sn22).
This third paragraph uses Level 3 (Compact Subparagraph / Archival Note Scale)—ideal for field timestamps, botanical citations, and understated contextual asides.

blocks.title: Ordered Tabular Sequence List
paragraphs: Setting titleLevel: 3 renders a compact H4 heading paired here with a staggered numbered sequence:

items: Morning River Rinse: Raw cotton hanks are washed in soft river water before sunrise.
Lane Stretching: Forty-yard warps are tensioned between granite posts along shaded village streets.
Natural Brush Sizing: Twin artisans walk the warp with palmyra-fibre brushes to seal every thread.
Pit-Loom Drafting: Extra-weft temple borders are lifted pick by pick from family memory.

blocks.text: Places tell you where you are. Stories tell you how it was. People tell you why it matters.
To travel by country canoe is to read an estuary at the speed of the lunar tide rather than the highway.
Every handwoven border carries the quiet signature of a watershed, a harvest season, and a household’s spoken memory.
When travellers sit beside our pit loom and understand the count of the cotton, they no longer bargain—they become lifelong patrons of our family’s name.
When patronage flows directly to the courtyard studio, young apprentices see a dignified future in inherited craft.

paragraphs.text: Callout blocks sit flat inside the editorial column in either Cream or Blue tints, supporting any combination of headers, rich-text paragraphs, titled checkmark lists, and titled numbered lists.

blocks.title: Visiting Working Craft Ateliers
blocks.subtitle: Practical rhythms & cultural etiquette along the Nila basin
blocks.text: Master weavers and bell-metal smiths welcome guests into active domestic courtyards rather than staged showrooms. Planning around morning light and monsoon humidity ensures an unhurried exchange.

unorderedList.title: What to Keep in Mind
items: Footwear is customarily left at the outer stone step (padippura) before entering loom verandahs.
Ask your host scholar before photographing sacred warp motifs or family shrines.
Carry breathable cotton attire suited for warm charcoal-and-clay casting sheds.

orderedList.title: How a Hosted Studio Dialogue Unfolds
items: Morning Tea & Context: Arrive before 9:30 AM when street-sizing and loom drafting are active.
Material Walkthrough: Examine raw hank cotton, natural dyestuffs, and pure kasavu threads alongside the maker.
Direct Patronage: Commission bespoke weaves directly from the household ledger with zero intermediary markup.

blocks.title: Seasonal Ritual Calendar of North Malabar
paragraphs: Sacred grove invocations across Kannur and Kasaragod follow the traditional solar calendar (Kollavarsham), opening after the northeast rains in late October.

items.title: Accompanied Entry:
items.text: Visits are hosted by community custodians who contextualize oral lineages.

items.title: Intimate Scale:
items.text: Courtyard gatherings are capped at four travellers to preserve sanctity.

blocks.title: Compact Highlights Shorthand (Default Blue Surface)
items: Cap studio visits at two small groups per week per household to prevent host fatigue.
Separate educational honorariums from retail sales so artisans never feel pressured to perform.
Maintain long-term post-journey shipping support for bespoke slow-woven commissions.

blocks.title: The Quiet Geometry of Street-Sizing
blocks.imageAlt: Morning warp preparation in a Kuthampully weaver lane
blocks.caption: Sticky desktop tracking keeps this 3:4 portrait anchored beside multi-paragraph prose.
paragraphs: Long before pit looms begin their rhythmic clatter indoors, entire lanes wake together to stretch forty-yard cotton warps between granite posts.
Walking slowly with two master brush-makers reveals how tactile memory guides every pass—adjusting tension by hand as humidity shifts across the valley.
Because guests arrive in groups of two or three rather than tour coaches, conversations unfold naturally over black chukku kaapi without interrupting morning work.
